task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-01, in the area of player absence and offensive reorganization):
The teammate with the closest pre-absence initiation profile (or most minutes / initiations / same-position minutes) is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=148; 148 spells; 11 cases

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: Can the closest-profile teammate be identified and shown to be the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types?
Are 11 absence cases (148 spells) enough for a test, given that spells within a case are not independent?
Do play-type initiation measures have enough exposure and reliability to define profiles and gains?
Does selecting the closest-profile teammate after observing the absence introduce regression to the mean?
Are the play-type labels derived from play-by-play outcomes, so that the gain measure leaks outcome information?

historical_evidence.finding: Tested whether, after an elite creator's signature action, teammates score more on the next k possessions with the same lineup. All 8 creators at horizon 0. Jokic lag-1 ATT=+0.0282 CI[-0.043,+0.099] p=0.3779, recorded as a clean null on teammate PPP. Recorded as adequately powered (Jokic lag-1 n=1880; Giannis n=1804; Doncic n=325). A secondary Antetokounmpo result (+0.075 distinct initiators, perm p=0.0002, BH 0.003) is recorded only as a 'structure not eff' cut. Validation status recorded as no_validation_recorded.

Connector absence versus usage-matched non-organizer absence on team offensive identity (D_A). Unmatched connector vs role D_A 0.2020 vs 0.1021, t=5.97 p=2.87e-08. Usage-matched paired dD_A +0.1151, P(conn>ctrl)=81.2%, t=6.35 p=7.35e-09, n=96 matched pairs. Recorded as limited by small sample and carrying MECHANICAL_FLOOR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks. Concerns identity disruption, not which teammate gains the absent player's initiations.

Catalogue of same-player and teammate X->Y sequential PPP premiums (for example P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560, n=31, t=+2.2). Most cells recorded as DIRECT. Recorded as limited by label or classification error and small sample. It is a descriptive catalogue, not a test of absence-driven redistribution.

Teammate DRIVE preceding PNR. League-wide with calibrated PNR labels, +0.022 PPP, p=0.004 (n~180k). Inferrer-only ATT=-0.006, p=0.76. Recorded as artifact: the effect vanished once PNR labels were restricted to inferrer-only, attributed to calibrated-PNR temporal contamination. Recorded as limited by label or classification error, with a LABEL_ERROR risk.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a teammate-PPP lift from an elite creator's signature action, lineup-matched, at lags 1-3.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an adequately powered null (B_powered_null): no elite creator produced a positive lineup-matched teammate-PPP lift at any lag. Shows that teammate-gain effects tied to creator actions were not detected in this data.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a PPP premium for teammate DRIVE-then-PNR sequences using play-type labels that included calibrated PNR labels.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact: the apparent +0.022 effect came from calibrated-label temporal contamination and disappeared (-0.006, p=0.76) under inferrer-only labels. Play-type labelling is a documented failure point.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Ranking extreme same-player and teammate play-type sequence premiums as an effect catalogue.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear (mechanism unclear), limited by label or classification error and small sample. Top and bottom cells were not stable enough to interpret as effects.

evidence_establishes: Play-type-based teammate PPP effects derived from this play-by-play are fragile. An apparent effect ([prior work][prior work]) disappeared under stricter labelling, and an adequately powered lineup-matched test ([prior work][prior work]) was null.
Small-sample play-type sequence premiums were not interpretable (FAM:[prior work]), so per-player, per-sequence estimates from this data are noisy.

A related absence-based question, connector absence on team identity, produced a supported result with a large usage-matched contrast ([prior work][prior work]). Matching on usage was a workable design element for absence comparisons.
evidence_does_not_establish: None of the retrieved records tests whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary play types. No retrieved record reports on this estimand.
No retrieved record gives a validated estimate of profile-closeness, selection rules, or gain magnitude after absence of a specific player.
[prior work] do not show whether 11 absence cases with 148 spells can support a ranked teammate-gainer comparison.
Validation status is not recorded for [prior work][prior work] or [prior work][prior work].
own_inferences: The effective sample is about 11 absence cases, not 148 spells. Spells within a case share the same absent player, teammates and lineup context, so spell-level tests overstate information.

Choosing the teammate with the closest pre-absence profile, then checking whether that teammate gains most, combines a post-hoc selection with the outcome. Regression to the mean could make the highest-gain teammate look close simply because of noise in the profile.
Three possible closeness criteria (profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) create a researcher-degrees-of-freedom problem unless one is fixed in advance.

Play-type primary types and gains are both computed from play-by-play initiator records, so the absent player's primary-type definition may be correlated with the outcome. Gains may partly reflect how types were assigned.
uncertainties: Whether the 2025-26 partial season data (regular season before 2026-04-13, playoffs before 2026-06-21) are included, and how they are handled, is not stated.
The number of absence events in each season, and whether the 11 cases are players or player-season episodes, is not stated.
Exposure of each teammate to the absent player's primary types before and after absence is unknown.
No retrieved record gives the reliability of play-type initiation measures at the per-player, per-season level.
Retrieval returned four families, none matching the question directly. Further [tool] calls were not run.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not answer the question, but they show that play-type-derived teammate PPP effects have been artifacts ([prior work][prior work]) or null under adequate power ([prior work][prior work]), and that play-type catalogues on small samples are not interpretable (FAM:[prior work]). With 11 cases and a post-hoc closest-profile selection, the historical failure pattern supports not running the test as posed. The supported connector-absence result ([prior work][prior work]) suggests a usage-matched absence design could be reused as a minimum viable test.

blocking_constraints.text: 11 absence cases is too few for a ranked comparison among several teammates. Spells within a case are not independent.
Choosing the closest-profile teammate after observing absence, then testing whether that teammate gains most, is subject to regression to the mean and selection on the outcome.
Primary play types and gains are both derived from play-by-play initiator records, so the gain measure may be partly determined by the label definition.
Per-teammate initiations in the absent player's primary types may be too sparse in 11 cases to rank teammates reliably.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved study tests whether the closest-profile teammate is the largest gainer in the absent player's primary types. The nearest records cover teammate PPP after creator actions (null, [prior work][prior work]), connector absence and identity (supported, [prior work][prior work]), play-type sequence premiums (descriptive, FAM:[prior work]), and a labelling artifact ([prior work][prior work]). These inform design risks and one reusable design element, but do not answer the question.

risks.text: 11 absence cases; 148 spells are clustered within cases, so effective n is far below 148 and a ranked comparison among teammates will be underpowered.
Closest-profile teammate chosen from noisy pre-absence measures and then judged on post-absence gain; regression to the mean will favour apparent gainers.
Primary types and post-absence gain both come from the same play-by-play initiator records; circularity inflates apparent gains.
Derived play-type labels can be contaminated by calibration and temporal assignment, as in [prior work][prior work].
Per-teammate initiations in each primary type may be too few for reliable profile estimates, as seen in the small-n cells of FAM:[prior work].
Initiation profiles and minutes-based closeness may not be reliable across seasons; reliability has not been established.
Lineup, minutes, role changes and opponent strength during absence can change teammate initiations independently of closeness.
Several closeness criteria (profile, minutes, initiations, same-position minutes) and several play types create many comparisons.
Without placebo absences or matched non-absence windows, the gain cannot be separated from ordinary teammate usage drift.
Seasons from 2022-23 to 2025-26 and partial 2025-26 data differ in roster and pace, so pooling risks drift artifacts.

design.estimand: As posed, the estimand is not well defined. Minimum viable estimand: among teammates ranked by a single pre-specified closeness criterion, the mean change in initiations for the absent player's primary play types, comparing absence spells with usage-matched non-absence windows.
design.unit: Team-player-spell (one absent player's spell, one teammate, one primary play type), with spells clustered by absence case.
design.sample: 11 absence cases from the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season and playoffs data, using only complete seasons (2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21).
design.power: Not estimable with 11 cases; a power analysis must be run before any test. Expect the ranking test to be underpowered, so report effects with intervals rather than a pass/fail test.
design.controls: Pre-specify one closeness criterion (for example pre-absence initiation profile, computed over a fixed window separated from the absence). Match on usage, minutes, lineup and position. Use split-half reliability of initiation profiles. Use labels restricted to inferrer-only calls as in [prior work][prior work].
design.falsification: Placebo absences from matched non-absence windows; a random-teammate placebo; and a test that the closest-profile teammate does not gain more than the nearest-usage teammate under the same matching.
design.multiplicity: Single pre-registered closeness criterion and single primary play-type definition for the confirmatory test; other criteria reported as exploratory with a multiplicity correction.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to a confirmatory test only if split-half reliability of the profile measure and the placebo test both pass pre-registered thresholds. Otherwise report the question as untestable with this data.
design.data_version: Complete-season NBA 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs; 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13; 2025-26 playoffs after 2026-06-21. Partial-season files excluded.
